skill.name: rdkit
skill.description: Advanced RDKit cheminformatics guidance for parsing molecules, calculating descriptors, building fingerprints, searching substructures, running similarity workflows, and creating molecular visualizations.
skill.summary: Use RDKit for molecular analysis, filtering, similarity search, descriptor calculation, and visualization.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives from Markdown fences, RDKit SMARTS bracket syntax, Python dictionary keys(), and explicit output-file writes in example scripts. No prompt injection, hidden network activity, credential access, or system reconnaissance was found, but SKILL.md includes unsafe pickle.load guidance that should be corrected.

remediation.suggestion: Replace the pickle load example with SDF, SMILES, or another safe format, or state that pickle files must only come from trusted sources.

remediation.issue: Output scripts can overwrite user-supplied paths
remediation.suggestion: Check for existing output files and require an explicit overwrite option before writing CSV, SMI, SDF, or report files.
Keep examples clearly labeled as Python and avoid shell-like backtick formatting outside Markdown code spans.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe Pickle Loading Guidance
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md recommends pickling molecules for performance and then loading molecules.pkl with pickle.load. Python pickle can execute code when loading untrusted files, so the guidance needs a trusted-data warning or safer format.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The referenced section explicitly imports pickle and shows pickle.load on a local file. This is a known unsafe deserialization pattern if users apply it to untrusted molecule datasets.

content.value_statement: Cheminformatics work needs reliable molecule parsing, descriptors, fingerprints, and SMARTS patterns. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical RDKit workflows for analysis, filtering, similarity search, and visualization.
actual_capabilities: Explains RDKit molecule creation and file I/O for SMILES, SDF, MOL blocks, and InChI.
Shows descriptor calculations for MW, exact mass, LogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, QED, and ring counts.
Guides fingerprint generation and similarity scoring with Morgan, RDKit, MACCS, atom-pair, and torsion fingerprints.
Provides SMARTS substructure examples and a script for include or exclude filtering.
Covers 2D drawing, grid images, highlighting, 3D conformers, and geometry optimization.
Includes scripts for molecular properties, similarity search, and substructure filtering.
limitations: Requires RDKit installed in the user Python environment.
Does not validate chemical safety, synthesis feasibility, or regulatory status.
Large molecular libraries may need custom batching and resource controls.
Example scripts are templates and may need path validation before production use.

use_cases.title: Profile Lead Compounds
use_cases.description: Calculate descriptors, Lipinski status, QED, and ring properties for candidate molecules.

use_cases.title: Filter Compound Libraries
use_cases.description: Apply SMARTS include and exclude patterns to remove unwanted structures or select target motifs.

use_cases.title: Teach RDKit Workflows
use_cases.description: Explain molecule parsing, fingerprints, visualization, and sanitization with practical examples.

prompt_templates.title: Calculate Basic Properties
prompt_templates.prompt: Calculate MW, LogP, TPSA, HBD, HBA, QED, and Lipinski status for these SMILES: [paste SMILES]. Explain invalid entries.

prompt_templates.title: Screen Similar Molecules
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Morgan fingerprints to compare this query molecule against my local SMILES file. Report hits above 0.75 and explain the parameters.

prompt_templates.title: Build SMARTS Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Create include and exclude SMARTS patterns for my compound library. Include aromatic heterocycles, exclude PAINS-like groups, and explain each pattern.

prompt_templates.title: Design an RDKit Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible RDKit workflow for an SDF library. Include sanitization checks, descriptors, fingerprints, substructure filters, visualization, and exports.

output_examples.input: A researcher asks for drug-likeness properties for caffeine and aspirin.
output: The response summarizes molecular weight, LogP, TPSA, hydrogen-bond counts, QED, and Lipinski status.
Invalid or ambiguous structures are called out before interpretation.

output_examples.input: A chemist wants benzene-containing molecules from a SMILES library but no acyl chlorides.
output: The response proposes include and exclude SMARTS patterns.
It explains how to run the substructure filter and review matched molecule counts.

output_examples.input: A data scientist needs similarity hits for a query molecule.
output_examples.output: The response recommends a fingerprint type, similarity metric, threshold, and export format for ranked hits.

best_practices: Validate every parsed molecule before calculating descriptors or fingerprints.
Use trusted input files and prefer safer interchange formats over pickle for shared data.
Record fingerprint parameters, descriptor sets, and thresholds for reproducible results.
anti_patterns: Loading pickle files from unknown sources.
Treating invalid SMILES or failed sanitization as valid molecules.
Comparing similarity scores without recording fingerprint type and metric.

faq.question: Does this skill install RDKit?
faq.answer: No. It assumes RDKit is available and points to standard installation patterns when import fails.

faq.question: Can it process SDF and SMILES files?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance and scripts cover SDF, MOL, SMILES, and related molecule inputs.

faq.question: Can it generate molecular images?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers molecule drawings, grid images, highlighted substructures, and drawing options.

faq.question: Is it suitable for drug discovery analysis?
faq.answer: It supports early cheminformatics analysis, but it does not replace experiments or regulatory review.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex run the included scripts?
faq.answer: Yes, when RDKit is installed and the user provides local input files and output paths.

faq.question: How should I handle untrusted molecule files?
faq.answer: Use text-based formats when possible, validate parsed molecules, and avoid loading pickle files from unknown sources.
